The story is tightly woven, using the physical setting (a cold, rainy ferry crossing) to mirror the emotional distance between a mother and her returning son. Every detail and action—such as Jonas standing in the rain without a hat, Ilse silently pushing his suitcase out of a puddle with her foot, the brief mention of the stripped bed in the small room, and the memory of him as a child—serves to characterize their estranged yet deeply rooted relationship. The progression from awkward, clipped dialogue on the dock to the final, quiet gesture of reconciliation (inviting him into the dry wheelhouse) follows a logical and emotionally satisfying path.
